# A.C.E DELTA TECH — Advanced Thermal Materials & Engineering Supply

> A.C.E DELTA TECH supports multinational manufacturing supply chains with thermal interface materials, liquid metal TIMs, cooling fluids, advanced electronic materials, technical sourcing and application engineering support.

Website: https://acedeltatech.com/
Email: acedeltatech@gmail.com

## Business Positioning
- Serves multinational manufacturing supply chains, engineering teams, technical procurement departments and international trading companies.
- Target segments: automotive electronics, EV battery systems, AI server manufacturing, data center cooling, advanced electronics manufacturing.
- Target-account profiles (not claims of existing customers): Bosch, Autoliv, Apple, Tesla, Boyd, major Japanese trading houses, Taiwanese-owned factories operating internationally.

## Core Capabilities
- Thermal Interface Materials (TIMs)
- Thermal Grease, Thermal Paste, Thermal Gel
- Gap Fillers and Electronic Encapsulation Materials
- Gallium-Indium-Tin (Ga-In-Sn) Liquid Metal TIM (GaInSn)
- Propylene Glycol-Based Cooling Fluids (PG25)
- Underfill Materials for Electronic Interconnect Reliability
- Engineering Material Selection and Technical Sourcing
- International Engineering Sample Coordination

## Engineering Applications
- AI Servers and GPU Thermal Management — TIM selection for HPC, AI accelerators, server cooling
- Data Center Cooling Infrastructure — liquid cooling fluids and materials for AI power/cooling equipment
- Automotive Electronics and EV Batteries — thermal gels, gap fillers for assemblies and battery thermal management
- 5G/6G Communication Electronics — thermal interface and electronic materials for high-density hardware and PCBA

## Technical Knowledge
- Liquid Metal TIM: Ga-In-Sn (gallium-based alloy family); electrical conductivity, material compatibility, wetting behavior and containment must be assessed per application.
- Thermal Grease Pump-Out: displacement/migration of TIM from the contact region under thermal cycling and mechanical deformation.
- Thermal Paste Dry-Out: degradation from volatile-component changes, oil separation, aging or formulation-dependent mechanisms.
- Reliability Engineering factors: thermal resistance, bond line thickness, thermal cycling, electrical properties, substrate compatibility, long-term stability.
